FAMILY & FRIENDS · STORY 1

Noah

Two Homes, One Family
📖 Read

I have two homes. I stay with Mum during the week and with Dad at weekends. That means they don't both see everything I do. Sometimes I tell Dad about school and have to explain who someone is. Mum already knows because she heard the first part!

Mum sees me on most school days. She knows when I have a lot of homework or feel tired after swimming. Sometimes she asks about my day as soon as I get home. I usually need a snack first. Talking is much easier after something to eat!

Dad and I both enjoy sport. We talk about football, watch matches and spend time outside together. We don't always agree about the players. Dad can think someone played well, but I think someone else was better. We usually have a lot to talk about after a match.

I like seeing Dad at weekends, but I also want to see my mates. We sometimes need to make plans a little earlier. I can't always go straight to the park when they ask. They understand that, but they sometimes forget. I sometimes forget too!

My little brothers want to be part of everything. They're twins, but they don't always want the same things. One can want to build something while the other wants a different game. They both ask me to join them. I can't play two games at once!

They often show me their drawings and things they make. Sometimes I'm busy and ask them to wait. They don't enjoy waiting very much. But I like seeing how happy they are when I look. They can tell me a very long story about one small picture.

I enjoy being their big brother. I can help them do things and teach them new games. Sometimes they copy me, which can be funny. It also means I have to be careful. Mum isn't happy when all three of us start shouting in the house!

My mates know my brothers too. I like it when they say hello and ask the twins a question. It only takes a minute, but the twins love it. Then my friends and I can spend time together. We don't always want two extra players.

I can talk to my friends about school, sport and problems. Sometimes I feel angry about something and just want to tell someone. They don't have to fix it. They can listen or make me laugh. I try to do the same when they have a bad day.

I'm different things to different people. I'm a big brother at home and one of the group with my mates. With Mum and Dad, I can still ask for help myself. I like that. Being thirteen doesn't mean I know how to do everything. Not yet, anyway!

FAMILY & FRIENDS · STORY 2

Abby

My Closest Friends
📖 Read

My three best friends are Sophie, Lily and Grace. We know a lot about each other. We can usually see when someone is happy or having a bad day. Sometimes they know something is wrong before I say anything. It's difficult to hide things from them!

Sophie finds it easy to talk to new people. I sometimes need longer to think of something to say. I like having her with me in a new place. She can start a conversation, and I can start talking when I feel ready. That helps a lot.

Lily makes me laugh. She sees funny things and tells us about them. We can laugh about one little thing for the rest of the day. Sometimes we remember it during a lesson. Then we have to try very hard to be quiet. That isn't always easy!

Grace is good to talk to when I'm worried. She listens and doesn't laugh at my problems. I can tell her things that I don't want everyone to know. I listen to her too. I don't want every conversation to be about me and my problems!

We don't agree about everything. Sometimes we want to watch different films or go to different places. Someone can get angry, but we're still friends. We have to talk and find a plan we all like. We usually find one after a little time.

Messages can be difficult too. I sometimes read a short message and think someone is angry with me. Then I worry and read it again. Often, the person is just busy! I'm trying to ask when I don't understand. That's better than worrying about it all evening.

At home, Mum often sees when I'm quiet. She asks me questions, but Sometimes I want a little time before I answer. Later, I might tell her about my day. It's easier when I have a little time first. Then I can explain what happened and how I feel.

Dad likes telling jokes. Some are funny, and some are very old. I enjoy laughing with him at home. When he tells my friends the same jokes, I feel different! I sometimes ask him to stop. He usually understands, but he often makes one last joke first.

My parents don't always understand problems with my friends. Sometimes a small thing feels very big to me. They ask questions, and I try to explain. I like knowing I can tell them if something really bad happens. I don't have to find every answer myself.

I smile a lot, but I'm not happy every minute. Sometimes I'm tired or worried and don't want to talk much. My family and friends know that. They still want to spend time with me. I can laugh with them, but I can also have a quiet day.

FAMILY & FRIENDS · STORY 3

Ameena

Our Busy Home
📖 Read

There's almost always someone to talk to in my family. There are lots of us, so our house can be very busy. Sometimes I'm trying to have one conversation and can hear two others. I don't always know who everyone is talking to. It can be quite funny!

I've got older and younger brothers and sisters. With the younger ones, I sometimes feel older than thirteen. They ask me questions and need help with things. With the older ones, I'm still a little sister. Sometimes I ask them exactly the same questions. We all need help with something.

My older sister knows what life in our house is like. I don't have to explain everything to her. I can tell her about a problem, and she usually understands. But she doesn't always agree with me. Being my sister doesn't mean she thinks I'm always right!

My younger brothers and sisters often want to show me things. Sometimes I'm busy, and they ask again and again. I can get angry when I'm trying to finish some work. They aren't always trying to be difficult. They're excited and want me to look.

I try to help my parents because they work hard. But I have my own plans too. Sometimes I want to meet my friends, and they need me at home. I like it when we talk about plans earlier. Then I know what I can and can't do.

Having a big family can be tiring, but there are good things too. Someone can make me laugh after a difficult day. Someone else can help me find a lost book. We don't all agree, but we can still help each other. I really like that about us.

With my friends, things are different. I don't have to help anyone get ready for school. I can talk about things I enjoy and listen to their news. Sometimes we talk about something serious. Often, we just laugh about something silly. Both are nice after a busy day.

I've got quite a few friends. I don't talk to all of them about the same things. Some enjoy running games. Others like sitting and chatting. I can have fun with different people. We don't all need to have exactly the same interests to be friends.

I like talking, and I usually have something to say. Sometimes I need to stop and listen more! A quiet friend might need longer to answer a question. I try to wait instead of starting another conversation. I want to hear what they think too.

I sometimes want more time on my own. That doesn't mean I want a different family or different friends. I enjoy our busy home and the people in my life. I just need a break sometimes. After a quiet moment, I'm usually ready to join everyone again.

FAMILY & FRIENDS · STORY 4

Luca

Different Friends, Different Sides
📖 Read

I think I'm pretty lucky when it comes to friends. I've got school friends, volleyball friends, swimming friends and friends I see on holiday. They're all a little different, but that's what makes it fun!

Of course, there's my family too. I live with my mum, dad and my little brother Oliver. He's ten, and he can be annoying, especially when he comes into my room without knocking. But we actually get along quite well.

Dad loves sports and being outdoors. Mum keeps everything organised. With school, volleyball, hockey and swimming, there's always something happening! Oliver and I sometimes watch each other's matches, and we both enjoy going to the swimming club.

At school, I spend a lot of time with my best mates, Jack and Harry. They know almost everything about me, even embarrassing things! We talk, laugh or just hang out. With them, even a boring afternoon can be fun.

My volleyball friends are different. We train together and know how to work as a team. Matches can get quite serious, especially when we're losing, but afterwards we're usually laughing again. Some teammates have become good friends outside volleyball too.

Then there are my friends from the swimming club. My family and I go there for an hour every week. It's not about winning races or being the fastest. We just swim, relax and enjoy ourselves. I've become friends with boys and girls my age there. Sometimes we play games in the water, and sometimes we just chat.

What I really like is that these groups sometimes mix. My school, volleyball and swimming friends all live in the same town. We meet in the park or at someone's house. Not everyone knows each other at first, but they soon start talking. Sometimes people who met through me become friends themselves. I think that's pretty cool!

My school friends and some of my volleyball friends also know that our swimming club and the campsite we visit in France. They know those places are a little different from what they're used to. Some think it's pretty cool that my family goes there. They sometimes ask questions, but they just accept me as I am.

And then there are my summer friends. Every year, my family goes to the same campsite in France. Some families return every summer, so I've known boys and girls there for years. We only see each other at the campsite in summer, but when we meet again, it feels like we've never been apart.

During the year, we keep in touch online. I don't spend all day on my phone, but I enjoy their messages. Sometimes we arrange to meet during another school holiday, perhaps for a day at a theme park. It's great not having to wait until summer!

The funny thing is that my friends know different sides of me. My school friends see me every day, my volleyball friends know me as a teammate, my swimming friends see me relax, and my camping friends know me from summer. But they're all important to me.

I don't think you need to do something exciting every time you see your friends. Sometimes just being together is enough. Whether I'm relaxing at home with my family or laughing with friends I haven't seen for months, I'm happy to have good people around me.

FAMILY & FRIENDS · STORY 5

Raheem

People Who Listen
📖 Read

I've got a few close friends, and I'm happy with that. I like knowing people well. With my best friends, I don't need to talk every minute. We can walk together or sit quietly for a while. That doesn't mean we're bored. We're just comfortable with each other.

Some of my friends talk much more than I do. I enjoy listening to their stories. Sometimes they're very funny, and sometimes I have a question. I like it when they give me time to ask it. I don't want to stop them in the middle of every sentence!

Being quiet doesn't mean I always agree. I've got my own ideas too. I sometimes need a moment to think before I speak. My friends know that. They also know I can make jokes. New people sometimes look surprised when I say something funny. Quiet people can laugh too!

I need more time with people I don't know. It's easier when we're doing something together. Then we have something to talk about. I can ask about the game or what someone likes. I don't need to know everything about a new person on the first day.

At home, Dad often enjoys my questions. We look at maps and talk about different places. Sometimes he knows the answer. Sometimes we both need to find out. I like doing that together. It's nice when an adult says they don't know something either.

Mum often thinks about the things we need. Dad and I can be talking about a place while she checks the time. We might need to eat or leave soon. I sometimes forget about that when something interests me. Mum tells us about the other things we need to do!

My sister likes knowing the plan. I don't always need to know what we're doing next. That can be difficult when we're going somewhere together. I might stop to look at something while she wants to keep walking. I understand why she gets a little angry sometimes.

We have good times together as well. She can make me laugh, and she sees things I miss. I like hearing what she thinks, even when it's different from my idea. We don't have to agree about everything. Sometimes we can even choose a film without talking about it for a long time!

I like our conversations at home. Someone asks a question during dinner, and everyone has an answer. I listen before I say much. Sometimes I hear someone else's answer and think it's better than mine. Sometimes I still think my first answer is right. Both can happen.

My family and friends know that I don't always talk a lot. They usually let me be quiet. If they think something is wrong, they ask. I like that. And when I do want to talk, I know someone will listen. That's important to me, even if I don't say it often.

FAMILY & FRIENDS · STORY 6

Mia

Being Myself
📖 Read

I'm quite quiet at school, but my family and close friends know another side of me. With them, I can talk a lot and make jokes. I need to feel comfortable first. Then it's much easier to say what I think. I've usually got a lot to say!

Mum and Dad know I sometimes need a little time after school. I don't always want lots of questions when I get home. Later, I might start talking while we're making food. That's often easier than sitting down for a special conversation. We can do something and talk.

Sometimes I don't know why I'm upset at first. I start explaining my day and slowly find the words. My parents can help by listening and waiting. I don't need them to ask five questions at once. One question is enough to start with!

They help me with everyday things too. They tell me to check my bag, finish my homework or look at the time. I don't always like that. Sometimes I think I know what to do and then forget anyway. That makes me angry with myself. Mum and Dad can get tired too.

I like doing things myself when I can. If I need help, I don't always need someone to do the whole job. They can show me the first part or help me find something. Then I can try the next part. I feel good when I can do it.

My close friends know I sometimes start talking about something else. Something in their story gives me another idea, and I start talking about that. Then I forget the first story! They can help me remember. We usually laugh about it, but I try to listen carefully too.

A big group can be more difficult. A few people are talking, and I don't know when to start speaking. When I'm ready, they're often talking about something else. I like it when a friend asks what I think. Then I have a chance to answer.

Spending time with one friend is often easier. We can listen to music or do something together. I don't have to speak louder than everyone else. We don't have to hurry when we talk. I can tell my story, and my friend has time to listen.

I want to be a good friend too. I care when someone is sad or worried. Sometimes I start speaking before the end of their story. I want to be kind. I try to stop, say sorry and listen to the rest. Their news is important to me.

My family and friends don't understand me every time. I don't always explain things well either. But we can talk again if something goes wrong. I like knowing that one mistake doesn't change everything. I can be myself, ask for help and have fun with the people I love.
